title: Typed routes not working in Expo 51 and Expo router
body:
### Minimal reproducible example

https://github.com/reporter/typed-routes

### What platform(s) does this occur on?

_No response_

### Did you reproduce this issue in a development build?

No (tested in Expo Go)

### Summary

Creating a new project with `yarn create expo-app` (Expo 51) seems to have broken the typed routes for expo router. When I downgraded to Expo 50 (and `npx expo install --check`), typed routes started to working again. I guess there's something wrong with the generation of the types when the development server starts 🤔

Also having this issue... we were previously using `import type { AllRoutes } from 'expo-router';`

As @reporter mentioned, SDK 51/expo-router update made a change to the generated types to be:

`export namespace ExpoRouter {`

instead of 

`declare module "expo-router" {` that it has in SDK 50.

We were able to move forward by instead importing the namespace using: 
`import type { ExpoRouter } from 'expo-router/types/expo-router';` and using `ExpoRouter.AllRoutes` or `ExpoRouter.LinkProps` etc

However this **doesn't** fix the typing of the routes

```ts

const route: ExpoRouter.AbsoluteRoute = 'any-wrong-path-which-ts-doesnt-care-about';
```

so it looks awful, and doesn't include any actual route typings.

```diff
diff --git a/build/typed-routes/generate.js b/build/typed-routes/generate.js
index 1e621830d26f90b3105d326ae31690c1e51730d1..01cce851540fd8d8882181ede0ec8fb2b3f22c38 100644
--- a/build/typed-routes/generate.js
+++ b/build/typed-routes/generate.js
@@ -26,7 +26,7 @@ function getTypedRoutesDeclarationFile(ctx) {
     return (node_fs_1.default
         .readFileSync(path_1.default.join(__dirname, '../../types/expo-router.d.ts'), 'utf-8')
         // Swap from being a namespace to a module
-        .replace('declare namespace ExpoRouter {', `declare module "expo-router" {`)
+        .replace('export namespace ExpoRouter {', `declare module "expo-router" {`)
         // Add the route values
         .replace('type StaticRoutes = string;', `type StaticRoutes = ${setToUnionType(staticRoutes)};`)
         .replace('type DynamicRoutes<T extends string> = string;', `type DynamicRoutes<T extends string> = ${setToUnionType(dynamicRoutes)};`)
```

comments.author: participant35
comments.body:
Building upon the patch by @participant28, I think I got it working correctly!

```patch
diff --git a/build/typed-routes/generate.js b/build/typed-routes/generate.js
index 1e621830d26f90b3105d326ae31690c1e51730d1..a42ca3886501c1636640e75e83a87eff3bcc3ce4 100644
--- a/build/typed-routes/generate.js
+++ b/build/typed-routes/generate.js
@@ -26,7 +26,12 @@ function getTypedRoutesDeclarationFile(ctx) {
     return (node_fs_1.default
         .readFileSync(path_1.default.join(__dirname, '../../types/expo-router.d.ts'), 'utf-8')
         // Swap from being a namespace to a module
-        .replace('declare namespace ExpoRouter {', `declare module "expo-router" {`)
+        .replace(`import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
+import type { TextProps, GestureResponderEvent } from 'react-native';
+
+export namespace ExpoRouter {`,
+          `declare module "expo-router" {\n  import type { ReactNode } from 'react';\n  import type { TextProps, GestureResponderEvent } from 'react-native';\n  export * from "expo-router/build";`
+        )
         // Add the route values
         .replace('type StaticRoutes = string;', `type StaticRoutes = ${setToUnionType(staticRoutes)};`)
         .replace('type DynamicRoutes<T extends string> = string;', `type DynamicRoutes<T extends string> = ${setToUnionType(dynamicRoutes)};`)
```

comments.author: participant21
comments.body:
@participant40 

The way you structured your screens is very unconventional. Usually in the file-system routers they expect you to structure your files and folders like how you'd structure URLs.

As for Expo Router, it should be in the `app` directory, and by convention you should use kebab-case (lower-case file and folder names and separate them by dashes).

I highly suggest you to look at the docs [here](https://docs.expo.dev/router/create-pages/).


Things I would check for if I were you:
1. Making sure I've `export default`(ed) the screens I want to use.
2. If it still doesn't show up, making sure to define the screens in the `_layout` file with their paths in case Expo Router doesn't recognize your convention.
3. If you have time, maybe try to restructure your folder structure to match the convention everyone uses.

comments.body:
I think I'm experiencing another issue with this when you have nested layouts and static routes. I was seeing the prefix of the route being dropped and I needed to apply this patch https://github.com/participant43/haohao.how/blob/149781fae327c14dd0a06d57b7144af31424d71d/.yarn/patches/expo-router-patch-c2c9a30c9c.patch

```
/_layout.tsx
/index.tsx
/foo/
/foo/_layout.tsx
/foo/bar.tsx
```

The route for `/foo/bar` was being output as `/bar` because when crawling the filesystem the route nodes `node.route` is made relative to the layout:

https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/cbb5828481fe05d423d6f248fc8aa20fa167c140/packages/expo-router/src/getRoutesCore.ts#L45
https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/cbb5828481fe05d423d6f248fc8aa20fa167c140/packages/expo-router/src/getRoutesCore.ts#L296

But in the typed routes generator the layout route is not put back:

https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/cbb5828481fe05d423d6f248fc8aa20fa167c140/packages/expo-router/src/typed-routes/generate.ts#L67

@participant47 

> Noticing similar issues, even with the patch, in a monorepo context — eg where the project-root is different the the workspace- / node_modules-root
> 
> Here's a [repro](https://github.com/participant47/nx-expo-router-repro-2024-05-25/tree/repro/typed-routes-monorepo-issue).

I think the issue here is probably that your patch isn't being applied. In your repo you have `patch-package` only being run in the root package.json, but you have the `@nx/expo` fixer scripts that copy the dependencies and devDependencies into the app package.json, but you didn't copy the post-install script that actually runs `patch-package`.

So I think in your case the issue is with your Nx stuff. BTW I'm using yarn workspaces too and don't need to do any workarounds, I just run `yarn` in the root before doing `eas build` or `eas update`, you can have a look here https://github.com/haohao-how/haohao.how/blob/95011bda5549777a88ec6c3eed3abbb5713757d6/.github/workflows/expo-eas-build.yml#L39
